metaDescription: Six poultry shears under budget compared: OXO take-apart blades, MAD SHARK 3.5mm steel, HENCKELS, DRAGON RIOT, Tingling and SimCoker, with dishwasher notes.
introParagraphs: This is the tier where poultry shears finally gain the features the cheaper models lack. The OXO Good Grips spring-loaded shears have blades that separate for cleaning, the MAD SHARK is forged from molybdenum-vanadium steel with 3.5mm blades and a thumb-activated lock, the DRAGON RIOT uses German stainless steel with micro-serrated edges, and the HENCKELS is a compact locking pair with serrated 3.5 inch blades. The Tingling and SimCoker remain as value options.

We evaluated the six listings on cleaning access, published steel facts, serration, lock design and handle grip. The compromise is that spending to the top of the range buys cleanability and edge design more than it buys raw power, since several listings now state dishwasher approval or separable blades while thickness is stated only by the MAD SHARK and the Tingling, both at 3.5mm.

The main decision at this tier is between three philosophies: take-apart cleaning with the OXO, a heavy forged blade with the MAD SHARK, and a compact brand-name tool with the HENCKELS. The sections below compare the six picks by name and number so you can match one to how you cook, how you wash up and how often you spatchcock.

products.name: MAD SHARK Heavy Duty Poultry Shears
products.description:
The MAD SHARK is forged from molybdenum-vanadium steel with precision-tempered 3.5mm blades, according to the listing. That matches the thickness often cited for poultry shears, and it makes this the strongest-specified pick in the lineup alongside the Tingling.

A spring-loaded design and a thumb-activated safety lock handle one-handed operation, and the listing says the lock engages in 0.2 seconds, a maker claim rather than a measurement. The title mentions dishwasher use and a non-slip handle, and the listing adds a built-in walnut-cracking feature. The first two facts are the ones that matter for everyday cooking.

In practice the thumb lock is the feature to value in a busy kitchen, because you can close and lock the shear without using your second hand. Compared with the Tingling, the MAD SHARK adds the molybdenum-vanadium steel claim, a thumb lock and a dishwasher mention at the same 3.5mm thickness. Against the OXO, it does not advertise blades that separate. Check the product page for exact dishwasher guidance before relying on it. If a thumb lock is new to you, practice closing and locking it with your thumb a few times before you reach for it with greasy hands.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want 3.5mm forged blades with a one-handed thumb lock.
pros: Dishwasher use mentioned in the listing
cons: Lock speed is a maker claim

products.name: OXO Good Grips Spring-Loaded Poultry Shears
products.description:
The OXO is the only pick in this guide whose listing says the blades separate for easy cleaning by hand or in the dishwasher. That is the solution to the biggest hygiene issue with poultry shears, which is residue trapped at the pivot after raw chicken.

The curved, tapered design is described as engineered to reach hard-to-access spots, and the stainless steel micro-serrated blades are notched to hold bones in place while you cut. The spring-loaded action and heavy duty construction round out the package. The listing does not publish a blade thickness, so you cannot compare it directly with the 3.5mm MAD SHARK or Tingling.

The curved blades help you follow the backbone of a bird instead of fighting it, and the serrations keep slippery bone from rotating away. Compared with the HENCKELS, the OXO is a larger, separable shear with serrations. Compared with the DRAGON RIOT, it gives you the take-apart design and brand ergonomics but without a stated steel origin. If cleaning confidence is your priority, this is the pick. When you reassemble the blades, confirm they close fully and lock before storing, since a partly seated pair is awkward on the next cut.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want blades that separate for cleaning and serrations that hold bone.
pros: Blades separate for hand or dishwasher cleaning
Micro-serrated blades hold bones in place
Curved tapered blades reach tight spots

products.name: DRAGON RIOT Heavy Duty Poultry Shears
products.description:
The DRAGON RIOT listing describes German stainless steel that is corrosion resistant and sharp, with micro-serrated blade edges that give non-slip cutting. It is also marketed as bigger and stronger than regular kitchen shears and as dishwasher safe, according to the title.

The ergonomic handles are described as soft and secure, and the shear is pitched for chicken and meat cutting as well as seafood. No blade thickness is stated, and the steel origin is a maker claim, so rely on the micro-serrations and dishwasher note as the practical details.

In the lineup, the DRAGON RIOT sits between the OXO and the MAD SHARK. It has serrations like the OXO but no separable blade, and it has dishwasher approval like the MAD SHARK but without a published 3.5mm figure. It is a good choice if you want grip on slippery bone and easy cleanup in one tool. If you often cook a whole turkey, the larger size relative to ordinary kitchen shears gives you a bit more reach into the cavity, though the listing does not give dimensions to compare with the OXO.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want serrated blades and dishwasher-safe cleanup.
cons: German steel wording is a maker claim

products.name: HENCKELS Kitchen Shears for Poultry
products.description:
The HENCKELS poultry shears are a compact, brand-name pair with 3.5 inch steel blades, serrated edges and locking blades for safe storage. The title lists dishwasher safety and heavy duty construction.

Note that 3.5 inches is a blade length, not a thickness, and the listing does not publish thickness. The serrations help the blade hold slippery bone, and the lock keeps the shears closed in a drawer. The listing describes the shears as 4 inch in total, so they are smaller than the OXO and the MAD SHARK.

The compact size suits a small kitchen drawer and a cook with smaller hands, though it offers less leverage on large birds. Compared with the DRAGON RIOT, the HENCKELS is a brand-name option with dishwasher approval and a lock. Compared with the OXO, it is not described as separable. Pick it for an everyday shear that is easy to store and clean. For a whole turkey or a large roasting chicken, step up to the MAD SHARK or OXO, since a 4 inch tool asks more of your wrist.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a compact, dishwasher-safe, locking pair.

products.name: Tingling Heavy Duty Poultry Shears
products.description:
The Tingling pairs reinforced 3.5mm 3Cr stainless steel blades with a spring-loaded assist and a one-touch safety lock. It is one of two picks here that publish a 3.5mm thickness, and it costs less than most of the others.

The listing mentions 7cm blades, suited to tasks such as splitting lobster tails and trimming. It does not advertise serrations, dishwasher approval or a separable pivot. You get the key spec and the spring, but you wash it by hand.

Compared with the MAD SHARK at the same 3.5mm, the Tingling gives up the thumb lock and the dishwasher mention. Compared with the OXO, it has no serrations or take-apart blades. It is the value pick for someone who wants to match the 3.5mm spec without paying for brand features. If you wash by hand anyway, the missing dishwasher note matters little, and the saved cost can go toward a pair of cut-resistant gloves or a good cutting board.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want published 3.5mm blades at a lower cost.
pros: Lower cost than most picks here
cons: No serrations or take-apart pivot mentioned

products.name: SimCoker Heavy Duty Poultry Shears
products.description:
The SimCoker listing describes 3CR14 stainless steel that is thicker and more corrosion resistant than usual, an anti-slip handle and a safety lock. The listing says it cuts meat, vegetables, fruits, noodles, seafood, pizza and barbecue food.

The thickness is described qualitatively rather than in millimeters, so it cannot be compared with the 3.5mm of the MAD SHARK or Tingling. The maker also calls the edge razor-sharp, which is a marketing claim.

The anti-slip handle is the feature to value for greasy work. Compared with the Tingling, the SimCoker gives up a published thickness in return for a handle claim. Compared with the OXO and HENCKELS, it has neither serrations nor dishwasher approval in the text we evaluated. It is the value pick for a cook who cares most about a secure grip. Because the listing offers no thickness, pair expectations with chicken pieces and light joints, not a daily spatchcock habit.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a locking heavy duty shear with an anti-slip handle.
cons: No serrations or take-apart pivot mentioned

buyingCriteria.explanation: Raw poultry residue gathers at the pivot, so separable blades are the best hygiene feature. The OXO lists blades that separate for hand or dishwasher cleaning. The others rely on dishwasher approval or hand washing. If you cook raw poultry weekly, the OXO's design is worth prioritizing. Note that some separable designs include a small internal spring, so check the product page for reassembly. A separable pair also stores in two pieces if you prefer, though you should keep the parts together.

Poultry shears are often near 3.5mm because thin blades flex against joints. The MAD SHARK and Tingling both state 3.5mm. The OXO, DRAGON RIOT, HENCKELS and SimCoker do not state a thickness. The HENCKELS lists 3.5 inch blades, which is length, not thickness. For spatchcocking, prioritize the stated 3.5mm.

Serrations hold slippery bone and skin so the blade does not slide. The OXO, DRAGON RIOT and HENCKELS list serrated or micro-serrated blades. The MAD SHARK, Tingling and SimCoker do not mention serrations in the excerpts we evaluated. If you often cut skin-on, bone-in pieces, serrations reduce slipping.

A lock keeps blades closed in storage and protects hands. The MAD SHARK has a thumb-activated lock, the Tingling a one-touch lock, the HENCKELS locking blades, and the SimCoker a safety lock. A thumb or one-touch lock can be operated with one hand, which matters when the other hand is holding a slippery bird. Test the lock after unboxing, because a stiff lock is a daily irritation.

Dishwasher approval simplifies cleanup. The MAD SHARK, DRAGON RIOT and HENCKELS mention dishwasher safety in their titles, and the OXO says blades can be cleaned by hand or in the dishwasher. The Tingling and SimCoker do not state it in the text we evaluated. A dishwasher can dull steel over time, so hand washing remains gentler.

A large shear gives leverage on big birds, while a compact one stores easily. The HENCKELS is the compact pick at about 4 inches overall, and the DRAGON RIOT is marketed as bigger than regular kitchen shears. The SimCoker lists an anti-slip handle and the DRAGON RIOT soft ergonomic handles. Match size to your largest bird and your hand size.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning access
howWeEvaluated.description: We prioritized listings that say the blades separate or that the shear is dishwasher safe. The OXO leads with separable blades, while the MAD SHARK, DRAGON RIOT and HENCKELS mention dishwasher use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Published steel facts
howWeEvaluated.description: The MAD SHARK and Tingling state 3.5mm blades. The MAD SHARK adds molybdenum-vanadium steel, the DRAGON RIOT German stainless steel, and the SimCoker 3CR14. We treated unpublished thickness as unknown.

howWeEvaluated.title: Edge and grip
howWeEvaluated.description: Micro-serrations on the OXO and DRAGON RIOT, serrated blades on the HENCKELS and an anti-slip handle on the SimCoker were compared for how they reduce slipping.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lock and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: The MAD SHARK has a thumb lock, the Tingling a one-touch lock, the HENCKELS locking blades and the SimCoker a safety lock. We weighed one-handed operation.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The MAD SHARK leads on published thickness with a thumb lock, the OXO on take-apart cleaning, the DRAGON RIOT on serrations with dishwasher approval, the HENCKELS on compactness, the Tingling on value with thickness and the SimCoker on grip value. We used specs and buyer feedback in broad terms and did not claim hands-on testing.

faq.q: Which pick is easiest to clean?
faq.a: The OXO, because its listing says the blades separate for cleaning by hand or in the dishwasher. The MAD SHARK, DRAGON RIOT and HENCKELS mention dishwasher use. Always dry the pivot afterwards, and keep a stiff brush for the serrations where raw poultry fat tends to cling.

The MAD SHARK or the Tingling, since both state 3.5mm blades. The OXO adds curved serrated blades that follow the backbone, though it does not publish a thickness. Choose by whether you value strength or cleaning access. The Tingling matches the thickness for less, while the MAD SHARK adds the thumb lock and a dishwasher mention.

It has 3.5 inch blades and about 4 inches overall, so it offers less leverage than the larger shears. It suits small hands and tight drawers. For large turkeys, choose a bigger shear. If space in the drawer is your real constraint, the HENCKELS lock keeps the blades closed while it sits next to other tools.

faq.q: Are the steel origin claims reliable?
faq.a: German stainless steel on the DRAGON RIOT and molybdenum-vanadium on the MAD SHARK are maker claims. Rely on the stated thickness, serrations and dishwasher notes as the practical details. Check the product pages for maker information. None of the listings supply hardness figures, so compare on thickness, edge style and cleaning design.

Serrations hold slippery bone and skin so the blade does not slide. The OXO, DRAGON RIOT and HENCKELS list them. They help most on bone-in, skin-on pieces. Plain-edge designs like the MAD SHARK rely on blade thickness and a tight pivot instead.

faq.q: Does a dishwasher harm poultry shears?
faq.a: Dishwasher heat and detergent can dull steel and loosen pivots over time even when a maker allows it. The OXO, MAD SHARK, DRAGON RIOT and HENCKELS all mention dishwasher use in some form, so it is permitted, but hand washing is gentler. Whichever you choose, dry the pivot and store the shears locked.

faq.q: What is the main thing this tier adds over cheaper ones?
faq.a: Cleaning access and edge design. The OXO's separable blades, the serrations on the OXO, DRAGON RIOT and HENCKELS, and the dishwasher notes on several listings are what the lower tier lacks. The 3.5mm thickness itself is already available from the Tingling, so extra spend is about hygiene and grip rather than raw cutting power, which suits a household that cooks poultry every week.

faq.q: Are separable blades safe to reassemble?
faq.a: Some designs include a small spring that can pop out during disassembly. Check the OXO product page for how the blades separate and rejoin. Take your time and keep the parts together. If a spring is involved, separate the blades over a towel so nothing bounces away.
